title: Diwali 2026 Places to Celebrate Across India
summary: Explore the best diwali 2026 places to celebrate, from Jaipur and Ayodhya to Varanasi and Amritsar, with practical travel planning advice.
body_markdown:
Diwali looks different from one Indian city to another. Jaipur turns its historic markets into a field of lights, Ayodhya is associated with large devotional celebrations, Varanasi brings the festival into its ghats and temples, while Amritsar observes the period through the distinct Sikh tradition of Bandi Chhor Divas.


In 2026, Diwali falls on Sunday, November 8. That makes the date especially important for travel planning because the festival does not automatically form a conventional long weekend. The best diwali 2026 places to celebrate are therefore not only about spectacle. They are also about travel time, crowd levels, the kind of celebration you want and how much leave you have.


# **Diwali 2026 Date and the Travel Question**


Diwali is on Sunday, November 8, 2026. The listed Lakshmi Puja muhurat for New Delhi is 5:54 PM to 7:50 PM, while Jaipur’s local timing is 6:03 PM to 7:59 PM.


The timing matters because a festival trip should not accidentally turn the main celebration into a transit window. If you want to celebrate in your destination, arrive early enough to settle in. If you want to be home for Lakshmi Puja, choose a destination that allows a comfortable return.


For the wider festival calendar, zingbus’s[2026 festival calendar](https://www.zingbus.com/blog/upcoming-festivals-in-india-complete-guide/) also places Diwali within the broader November festival period and highlights several major Indian travel corridors.


## **The Best Diwali Destinations Depend on the Experience**


There is no single national answer to the question of where Diwali is best. The festival is culturally broad enough that different destinations suit completely different travellers.


### **Ayodhya for a Large Devotional Celebration**


Ayodhya is one of the strongest choices for travellers who want a major public celebration with a strong religious context. The city’s association with Lord Ram gives Diwali a particular significance, and large-scale illumination and diya displays have become an important part of its recent festival identity.


The practical issue is crowd management. A major festival in a pilgrimage city can affect road movement, accommodation and access around important areas. Anyone travelling to Ayodhya should plan accommodation and transport early and allow more local travel time than a normal weekend would require.


The experience also rewards patience. The purpose is not to rush through several attractions between photographs. The atmosphere of the city and its devotional spaces is the main reason to be there.


### **Varanasi for Ghats, Temples and Ritual**


Varanasi gives Diwali a completely different physical setting. The old city, temple lanes and ghats create a dense atmosphere where lamps and religious observance are part of everyday life rather than a separate festival venue.


Keep the Varanasi itinerary simple because the city rewards time rather than speed. That becomes even more important around a major festival when walking routes, temple queues and ghat areas can become crowded.


There is also an important date distinction. Dev Deepawali is a separate later celebration associated strongly with Varanasi. A traveller searching for the famous later ghat illumination should not assume it takes place on November 8.


### **Jaipur for Lights, Markets and Heritage**


Jaipur is arguably the easiest choice for travellers who want the visual side of Diwali combined with a conventional city holiday. Johari Bazaar, Bapu Bazaar and the walled city become the centre of festive movement, while the surrounding forts and palaces give the trip a heritage dimension.


The city’s compact old-city cluster also helps with a short break. You can spend daytime hours at the major heritage sites and reserve the evening for the markets rather than crossing the entire city.


The[zingbus Jaipur travel guide](https://www.zingbus.com/blog/places-to-visit-in-jaipur/) is useful for building the non-festival part of the itinerary, particularly if you want to include Amber Fort, City Palace, Nahargarh Fort and the bazaars.


### **Amritsar for Bandi Chhor Divas**


Amritsar offers one of the most culturally distinctive festival experiences in the country because Diwali coincides with Bandi Chhor Divas in Sikh tradition.


The Golden Temple is central to the experience, but visitors should understand that this is a religious site first. Large crowds, security checks and queues are normal around important festival dates. Dress and behaviour should remain respectful, and travellers should avoid treating the celebration purely as a photography opportunity.


For travellers interested in religious and cultural history, Amritsar can be more meaningful than a destination chosen only for decorative lights.


### **Udaipur for a Slower Heritage Holiday**


Udaipur suits travellers who want Diwali to sit inside a broader heritage holiday. The city’s lakes, palaces, old-city ghats and evening atmosphere create a slower rhythm than a large pilgrimage celebration.


The current[zingbus Udaipur guide](https://www.zingbus.com/blog/tour-package-udaipur-city-of-lakes-retreat-guide/) notes that mornings work well for heritage visits, afternoons for lake and indoor experiences, and evenings for ghats, rooftops and cultural activities.


That rhythm makes Udaipur useful when you have three or four days rather than only a single festival evening.


### **Mysuru for a Southern India Perspective**


Mysuru is worth considering for travellers who want a southern Indian Diwali experience rather than repeating the better-known northern and western circuits.


The city’s royal heritage, markets and surrounding cultural attractions make it suitable for a longer trip. It is also a useful reminder that a Diwali travel guide should not treat the festival as a single North Indian event.


### **Delhi for Maximum Flexibility**


Delhi is the simplest choice if you want a festival atmosphere without committing to intercity travel. Markets, neighbourhoods, temples and residential areas all develop their own Diwali character.


The benefit is control. You can celebrate locally and use the days before or after the festival for a separate short trip, rather than trying to coordinate a distant destination around the main evening.


## **Diwali Destinations at a Glance**


**Destination** **Best For** **Travel Character**


Ayodhya Devotional public celebration High crowd and pilgrimage demand


Varanasi Ghats, temples and ritual Dense, walk-heavy city experience


Jaipur Lights, markets and heritage Compact cultural city break


Amritsar Bandi Chhor Divas and Golden Temple Religious and cultural experience


Udaipur Heritage and lakes Slower multi-day holiday


Mysuru Southern Indian culture Heritage-led longer trip


Delhi Flexibility and local celebration Minimal intercity travel


The comparison is useful because the destinations should not be treated as interchangeable. Your preferred festival atmosphere should determine the shortlist before transport is booked.


## **How to Choose the Right Diwali Destination**


Start with the question of where you want to be on Sunday evening. If you need to attend a family celebration at home, a destination that requires a long return journey on Sunday is a poor fit.


Next, consider crowd tolerance. Ayodhya, Varanasi and Amritsar can become extremely busy around major religious celebrations. Jaipur is also crowded, but its experience is more distributed across markets and the old city.


Finally, consider trip length. Jaipur can work in two or three days from Delhi. Udaipur is more comfortable with additional time. Varanasi and Ayodhya become easier when you allow room for queues and local movement.


## **Planning Transport Around Diwali**


Festival travel rewards early booking because both the main intercity leg and local accommodation can tighten as the date approaches.


zingbus already maintains destination and route content for several of these corridors. Before booking, use the relevant live city or route page rather than relying on an old timetable copied from a travel article.


For example, travellers planning Jaipur can check the current[Delhi to Jaipur bus route](https://www.zingbus.com/bus-tickets/delhi-to-jaipur-bus-route) , while a Varanasi plan can be built around the route options available for the selected travel date.


## **Do Not Confuse Diwali With Dev Deepawali**


This is one of the most important distinctions in a Varanasi-focused Diwali search. Diwali and Dev Deepawali are different festivals observed on different dates.


Diwali in 2026 falls on November 8. Dev Deepawali comes later around Kartik Purnima and is especially associated with the spectacular illumination of Varanasi’s ghats.


If your travel goal is the famous mass ghat illumination often shown in photographs of Varanasi, verify the exact festival date before booking. A search for “Diwali in Varanasi” can otherwise lead to confusion between two separate events.


## **Travel Tips for Crowded Festival Cities**


Arrive at bus boarding points earlier than usual because city traffic can become unpredictable. Keep your booking confirmations and identification easily accessible.


At religious sites, follow security instructions and expect queues. Avoid carrying unnecessary bags into crowded areas.


For market-heavy destinations such as Jaipur, decide on a meeting point if travelling with family or friends. Dense crowds can make mobile calls and visual contact difficult.


Most importantly, leave space in the itinerary. Festival travel is not the time to schedule six attractions across three neighbourhoods with exact arrival times.


## **The Best Diwali Destination Is the Right Match**


The diwali 2026 places to celebrate range from pilgrimage cities and religious centres to heritage destinations and modern metros. That variety is the strength of travelling during the festival.


Choose Ayodhya or Amritsar when religious significance is central. Pick Varanasi for its ghats and ritual atmosphere. Jaipur works for lights and markets, Udaipur for a slower heritage holiday, Mysuru for a different regional perspective and Delhi when flexibility matters most.


The destination becomes memorable when it matches the way you actually want to celebrate, rather than simply being the place with the biggest headline.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **When is Diwali in 2026?**


Diwali in 2026 falls on Sunday, November 8, with Lakshmi Puja timings varying slightly by city.


### **What are the best diwali 2026 places to celebrate?**


Ayodhya, Varanasi, Jaipur, Amritsar, Udaipur, Mysuru and Delhi are strong choices, depending on the celebration style you prefer.


### **Is Diwali 2026 a long weekend?**


Diwali 2026 falls on Sunday, so it does not automatically create a standard long weekend without additional leave.


### **Which city is best for Diwali in India?**


The best city depends on your preference: Jaipur for markets and lights, Ayodhya for devotion, Varanasi for ghats, and Amritsar for Bandi Chhor Divas.


### **Is Ayodhya good for Diwali 2026?**


Ayodhya is suitable for travellers seeking a large devotional celebration, but significant crowds and transport pressure should be expected.


### **Is Diwali celebrated in Varanasi?**


Diwali is celebrated in Varanasi with lamps, temple activity and festive decoration, while Dev Deepawali is a separate later celebration.


### **Is Jaipur a good place for Diwali?**


Jaipur is a strong Diwali destination for illuminated bazaars, heritage architecture, shopping and a lively old-city atmosphere.


### **What is special about Diwali in Amritsar?**


Diwali coincides with Bandi Chhor Divas, giving Amritsar a distinctive Sikh cultural and religious context during the festival period.


### **Is Udaipur worth visiting during Diwali?**


Udaipur is worth considering for travellers who want lakes, palaces, old-city experiences and a slower multi-day festive holiday.


### **Which Diwali destination works for a two day trip?**


Jaipur is particularly practical for a short trip from Delhi because the city has a concentrated heritage and market circuit.


### **Should I book buses early for Diwali?**


Yes. Festival demand can increase seat pressure and local traffic can make journey times less predictable.


### **Is Dev Deepawali the same as Diwali?**


No. Dev Deepawali is a separate later festival, especially associated with Varanasi and Kartik Purnima.


### **What should I check before booking a Diwali trip?**


Check the festival date, local celebration schedule, transport timings, accommodation location, crowd conditions and your return window.


### **How should I make a diwali 2026 places to celebrate travel plan?**


Start with the November 8 festival date, decide where you want to spend the main evening, then build transport, accommodation and leave around that priority.
